bib.title: OPT: Open Pre-trained Transformer Language Models

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; figure-only content (Fig 6/7 per-task curves, Fig 8-13 sample outputs) is not in the text.

question: Can a GPT-3-class suite of decoder-only language models (125M to 175B) be trained, matched to GPT-3 in quality, with less carbon, and shared openly with the research community?
hypothesis: OPT models trained with GPT-3 hyperparameters and current efficiency practice will roughly match GPT-3 on standard NLP tasks.
contributions: A suite of eight decoder-only transformers from 125M to 175B parameters
Release of models 125M-66B and access to OPT-175B on request
Release of the training logbook and the metaseq codebase
Evaluation on 16 NLP tasks, dialogue and responsible-AI benchmarks
Carbon estimate of about 1/7th of GPT-3

method.summary: Eight GPT-3-style decoder-only transformers are pre-trained on a roughly 180B-token English corpus (RoBERTa data, a Pile subset, PushShift Reddit) with AdamW, FP16 weights and FSDP plus Megatron tensor parallelism. OPT-175B ran on 992 A100-80GB GPUs with many manual restarts and learning-rate cuts. The models are evaluated with GPT-3 prompts on NLP tasks, plus dialogue and bias/toxicity benchmarks.
method.task: next-token pretraining of decoder-only language models

datasets.name: Pre-training corpus (RoBERTa subsets + Pile subset + PushShift.io Reddit)
datasets.split: random validation set of approximately 200MB held out, sampled proportionally to each dataset's size
datasets.source: BookCorpus, CC-Stories, CCNewsV2 (crawled to 28 Sep 2021), Pile subset (CommonCrawl, DM Mathematics, Gutenberg, HackerNews, OpenSubtitles, OpenWebText2, USPTO, Wikipedia), PushShift.io Reddit
datasets.preprocessing: MinhashLSH dedup at Jaccard >= .95; ad-hoc whitespace normalisation on Pile subsets; Reddit reduced to longest comment chain per thread (~66% smaller); GPT-2 byte-level BPE tokenizer; other Pile subsets dropped for causing gradient-norm spikes at 1.3B

datasets.name: 16 NLP tasks (HellaSwag, StoryCloze, PIQA, ARC E/C, OpenBookQA, WinoGrad, WinoGrande, SuperGLUE)
datasets.split: GPT-3 setup; CB 56, BoolQ 277, WSC 104 validation examples
datasets.preprocessing: WSC formulated as multiple choice following Brown et al. 2020

datasets.name: Dialogue: ConvAI2, Wizard of Wikipedia, Empathetic Dialogues, Blended Skill Talk, Wizard of Internet; MSC subset
ETHOS, CrowS-Pairs, StereoSet, RealToxicityPrompts, SaferDialogues, Safety Bench Unit Tests

other.note: NLP comparison uses numbers reported by Brown et al.; hate speech, CrowS, StereoSet, RTP use the Davinci API

training.objective: inferred: next-token (causal language modelling) loss; the paper does not name the loss
training.lr: peak LR by size 6.0e-4 (125M) to 1.2e-4 (175B), see Table 1
training.lr_schedule: linear warmup then linear decay to 10% of max LR over 300B tokens; OPT-175B required many mid-flight LR reductions (Fig 1)
training.warmup: 2000 steps in OPT-175B, 375M tokens in smaller baselines
training.batch_size: 0.5M to 4M tokens depending on size (Table 1), constant through training
training.steps: inferred: about 140k iterations for OPT-175B from the x-axis of Fig 1 and Fig 2
training.tokens: decay horizon 300B tokens; corpus is roughly 180B tokens; total tokens actually trained not stated
training.precision: model weights FP16, Adam state FP32, dynamic loss scaling
training.regularisation: gradient clipping at 1.0, lowered to 0.3 mid-flight; gradient predivide factor (two divisions by sqrt(N))
training.hardware: 992 80GB A100 GPUs, FSDP with Megatron-LM tensor parallelism, up to 147 TFLOP/s per GPU
training.compute: estimated 75 tons CO2eq for OPT-175B; GPU-hours not stated
training.wall_clock: about 2 months for OPT-175B including hardware failures

other.init: normal, mean 0, std 0.006; output-layer std scaled by 1.0/sqrt(2L); biases 0
other.hardware_failures: at least 35 manual restarts, over 100 hosts cycled, 70+ estimated automatic restarts
other.loss_divergence_recovery: lower LR and restart from earlier checkpoint with healthy loss scale (>=1.0) and downward-trending activation norms
other.other_midflight: tried vanilla SGD (plateaued, reverted to AdamW); reset dynamic loss scalar; switched to newer Megatron
other.carbon_note: with ablations, baselines and downtime, authors' own total cost estimate is roughly 2x higher (footnote 10)

inference.decoding: dialogue: greedy decoding up to 32 tokens; RealToxicityPrompts: nucleus sampling
inference.samples: RTP: 25 generations per prompt for 10,000 prompts
inference.prompting: NLP tasks: GPT-3 prompts and setup, 0/1/32 shots; dialogue: alternating 'Person 1:' and 'Person 2:' lines, no other prompt; ETHOS yes/no (binary) or yes/no/neither (multiclass)

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: NLP task accuracy; F1 omitted for MultiRC and ReCoRD

metrics.name: StereoSet LMS / SS / ICAT
metrics.definition: language modelling score, stereotype score, combined; normalised by token count not character count

metrics.name: Toxicity probability of continuation
metrics.definition: mean toxicity probability of continuations bucketed by prompt toxicity

eval.protocol: Single run per model; averages exclude MultiRC and WIC; no seeds or significance tests reported.

availability.weights: 125M-66B released; OPT-175B on request under non-commercial licence
availability.data: not distributed (datasheet only); component corpora are public

limits: No mitigations for toxicity or bias applied; authors call the technology premature for commercial deployment.
Evaluation setups may differ from Brown et al. (cannot replicate GPT-3 MultiRC via Davinci API); prompt and shot differences can change results.
Tiny validation sets (CB 56, BoolQ 277, WSC 104) make scale trends erratic.
Mid-flight changes could not be ablated; the carbon figure covers the final run, ablations/baselines/downtime roughly double total cost.
Carbon accounting is not standardised across the compared models.
Training-token count for OPT-175B is not stated directly: LR decays over 300B tokens against a ~180B-token corpus.
Models are English-dominant, older than Chinchilla-style data scaling; likely under-trained.
